newsitem.title: INDIA: Shares start lower on India national exchange.
newsitem.headline: Shares start lower on India national exchange.

text.p: Share prices started lower on Monday at India's National Stock Exchange (NSE) and are seen drifting with a sharp fall in the Dow Jones at the weekend discouraging fresh demand, analysts said.
"The Dow Jones tumble has affected the mood," said S.N. Satish, a fund manager at Lloyds Finance. "Fund managers are going to put fresh purchases on hold."
The market was unlikely to see a sell-off though, he said.
On Friday, the Dow Jones had slumped 247.37 points, or 3.1 percent, to 7,694.66 on a weakening dollar and worries on corporate earnings.
Traders said investors in India were also concerned about poor earnings forecast for companies in the first half of fiscal 1997/98 (April-March).
A recent Reuter poll showed profits are likely to grow by an average of 10.4 percent in the six months to September 30, compared to 12.2 percent in the year-ago period.
The market will undergo a re-rating after the results are announced in October, traders said.
"Overall, the undertone is weak," said independent analyst Arun Kejriwal. "The market has reached a stage where a correction is welcome."
The market is likely to offer bargains, he said.
"With every fall there's an opportunity," he said.
Traders attribute the market's weakness to a cooling after an eight week long rally.
"Far from an over-bought zone the market is hardly in a bought zone," said Bharat Shah, chief investment officer at Birla Capital International AMC Ltd.
"There's lot of money in the banks waiting to enter the markets which indicates that the market is substantially underbought as yet," he said last week.
At 0445 GMT, the NSE index was down 17.25 points, or 1.4 percent, at 1,210.65
